_comment: FROM-SCRATCH single-task baseline: same polymer_pool head, same DPA-3.3 descriptor ARCHITECTURE, but randomly initialised — no --finetune. This is the control arm for 'does pretraining/multitask replay help'. Descriptor + type_map are copied verbatim from input_polymer_pool.json so the arms differ ONLY in the weight init and the lr/steps schedule. See README 'From-scratch baseline'.

descriptor._comment: LOAD-BEARING here (unlike the finetune config, where --use-pretrain-script overwrites it from the ckpt). Identical to the finetune arm's architecture. skip_stat is deprecated and only forces fix_stat_std=0.3; kept as-is so both arms normalise identically.

fitting_net._comment: Identical to the finetune arm. dim_case_embd=0: no multitask branch to match (the multitask config needs 23 to agree with the energy branch). fparam is consumed RAW by polymer_pool.forward (it never applies fparam_avg/inv_std), so pre-standardized fparam behaves the same from scratch as in finetune.

learning_rate._comment: From scratch the descriptor is random, so it needs a higher lr for longer than the finetune arms (single-task finetune 1e-3/2000, multitask 2e-4/2000 to protect the shared descriptor). Not a controlled variable — a from-scratch run held to the finetune schedule would be a strawman.

training._comment: one polymer = one frame = one system, so batch_size is 1. 2x the finetune arm's steps: from scratch converges slower. Watch lcurve for val divergence — 591 polymers against a 16-layer/128-dim repflow WILL overfit, which is the point of the comparison.
